business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with Common Law-inspired corporate and maritime law elements
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty with the United States (entered into force 1991)
Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) with various jurisdictions
Double Taxation Agreement with South Korea (2021)
Partial Scope Agreement with Cuba and other ALADI instruments
Foreign Trade Agreement with the United States (TPA) (effective 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (as amended) on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing; Executive Decree No. 7 of 2021 (UBO registration); Law 70 of 2019 (Register of Final Beneficiaries); Law 52 of 2016 (beneficial ownership information) and Regulation No. 1-2016 of the Superintendency of Banks; regulatory guidelines issued by the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero, UAF)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificado de Registro de Sociedad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a contracting state to the Hague Apostille Convention; documents issued by the Public Registry are apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the designated authentication officer)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Estatutos de la Sociedad Anónima) notarized copy with certified Spanish translation if needed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of Panama (Notaría Pública) and the Panama Public Registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Firmeza o Solvencia) or Peace and Solvency Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Public Registry and the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in jurisdictions not adhering to the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the final beneficial owner registry filing (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales / RUBF certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Public Registry (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Residency for each UBO and legal representative (for banking/AML onboarding)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary or public authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and signatories against the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) Panamanian PEP list, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU consolidated sanctions list, and Interpol/domestic criminal watchlists; enhanced due diligence required for any person listed as PEP, associate, or high-risk correspondent; screening must be repeated at least every 90 days or upon any ownership or management change; records retained for at least 5 years after termination of business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Panama Public Registry – Electronic Portal (Registro Público de Panamá en Línea) accessible at www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All company names must be submitted in Spanish or in a Latin-script transliteration; foreign words are permitted only if transliterated into Latin alphabet without diacritics; the name reserves the exact graphic representation and may include acronyms and numerals; for corp slight naming, suffixes 'S.A.' or 'Corporación' or 'Sociedad Anónima' must appear; no translated name is accepted if it conflicts with an existing local registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a registry rejection notice (rechazo del nombre), the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the Dirección General de Registro Público (legalization office) within 10 business days of the rejection date; the petition must include the proposed name, the grounds of rejection, and a legal argument demonstrating that the name does not violate the applicable naming rules; if the reconsideration is denied, an appeal may be filed before the administrative tribunal (Tribunal Administrativo) within 5 business days. Simultaneously, the applicant may file a new name reservation with a distinct distinctive token without prejudice to the appeal. The standard reservation may be extended once upon payment of the applicable extension fee and if no opposition or conflicting prior application is registered.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for statutory compliance and mail forwarding purposes, provided that a resident Panamanian registered agent (Agente Residente) maintains the physical registered office address at a lawful corporate service provider office; for the hyper-casual mobile game publishing industry (ISIC 5820), virtual office only is acceptable for minimal substance and tax territoriality assessments, but robust commercial substance in connection with IP management, bank account opening, and AML rating may require additional physical presence and local payroll/back-office activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium (45%–55% risk for unannounced inspections) for entities holding bank accounts or benefiting from territorial tax exemption, especially where there is no local staff; the UAF, DGI, and the Public Registry conduct periodic and trigger-based audits of registered agent records and may request notarized evidence of commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama General Corporation Law, Ley No. 32 de 1927, as amended, Articles 1–207 (notably Articles 1–8 and 18–29 respecting corporate powers, capital, and registry filing); supplementary mercantile registration under the Código de Comercio of Panama and the regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General, Sección de Mercantil, Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución / Pacto Social y Estatutos (notarized Articles of Incorporation filed as the first testimonio).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under Ley No. 32 de 1927; at least one share must be issued and recorded as subscribed; capital may be paid in installments and no escrow or government bank-capital deposit is mandatory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS, the corporation was validly incorporated under Ley No. 32 de 1927; IT IS RESOLVED: (1) the shares subscribed and paid by the initial shareholder, as stated in the subscription list attached to the Escritura Pública, are issued and credited in the Share Registry; (2) the registered office located at the address indicated in the Articles of Incorporation is adopted, and the registered agent is retained; (3) the President, Secretary, and Treasurer are appointed, with authority to open bank accounts, execute game publishing and monetization agreements, and authorize all tax filings; (4) the Secretary is directed to obtain the RUC and any municipal Aviso de Operación; (5) all acts of the Incorporator prior to this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Certificación de Denominaciones (name-search module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name search presenting three ranked proposed corporate names. Pay the official search fee. Obtain the negative name certification and reserve the selected denomination for thirty days. After the reservation expires without incorporation, file a renewal or choose an alternate name.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused or marked homonymous, file a formal reconsideration with an alternate denomination; if the reservation lapses, submit a new application with the same name and wait for a new check.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (licensed Panamanian notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to prepare the Pacto Social y Estatutos in Spanish, including corporate purpose covering ISIC 5820 digital game publishing, capital provisions, share classes, registered agent acceptance, and director and officer provisions. The subscriber must execute the deed before the notary, who will read and attest the instrument.
required_dossiers: Stockholders' identities and credentials of the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires statutory corrections or clarification of the corporate purpose, amend the draft and present a re-executed deed before the same notary; if the registered agent refuses to accept, replace the agent before protocolization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Public Registry Fees and Documentary Stamps
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General del Registro Público / Banco Nacional de Panamá (approved payment windows)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate the inscription fee and documentary stamp taxes based on the authorized capital and deliver the fee schedule to the treasury window. Obtain the stamped payment receipt and attach it to the first testimonio. Preserve the original receipt for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Fee computation sheet prepared by notary or counsel
Power of attorney if fee payer is not the incorporator
Payment receipt in the name of the corporation's provisional identity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fee is recalculated and underpayment is detected, pay the difference plus any fines; if payment is misapplied, request a treasury correction and re-issue a matching voucher.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration at the Public Registry Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Mercantil, Archivo General
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first testimonio of the incorporation deed together with the stamped payment receipt. The registry examiner will review legality, verify the name certificate, assign the corporate folio, and inscribe the corporation. Request a certified copy of the inscription certificate.
required_dossiers: First testimonio of the Escritura Pública
Form in compliance with the Public Registry protocol
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry enters a suspension or preventive note, file the indicated corrective through a clarifying affidavit or undertake the necessary substitution or amendment; if the examiner demands a supplementary instrument, protocolize and present it without reopening the prior deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization of Corporate Books and Governance Ledgers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Legalization Office (Libros de Actas y Acciones)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, procure the Share Registry Book and Board and Stockholders' Resolutions Book. Each book must be opened and the first pages must be sealed and legalized at the Public Registry. Execute the first board resolution and enter share subscription and officer appointments.
required_dossiers: Copy of Articles of Incorporation with registry stamp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legalization office rejects the books due to incorrect pagination or binding, purchase compliant books and repeat sealing; if the minutes are signed after the deadline, file a statement of late registration if permitted under registry practice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the final public deed inscription and registered corporate documents to the RUC window. Obtain the corporate RUC number for ISIC 5820. The RUC must include the physical address and economic activity, enabling future tax payments, invoicing, and employer registrations.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Public Registry inscription
Corporate electronic identification or legal representative identification
Proof of physical address (leased office contract or title)
Power of attorney for tax agent if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RUC submission is queried for address or activity misclassification, file a modification statement before the same DGI registry; if the address certificate is missing, submit the signed lease and landlord's identification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and Complementary Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas; Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Concurrent to DGI registration, apply for the municipal Aviso de Operación for office-based software publishing. Obtain fire inspection clearance for office occupancy and, if required by the municipality, the Certificado de Uso de Suelo. The corporate headquarters must display the Aviso de Operación.
required_dossiers: Municipal forms and fee payment proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal taxador imposes inconsistent activity tariffs, appeal before the Alcalde with ISIC 5820 digital publishing characterization; if fire clearance is conditionally denied, post the required extinguishers, exit signs, and electrical certification and request re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección General de Rentas (licensing); Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) for general commercial activity; no industrial manufacturing board applies to ISIC 5820.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (municipal business operating permit); not an industrial manufacturing permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Normas y Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA registration because the activity is office-based digital publishing with no fixed industrial installation, no point-source atmospheric emissions, and no hazardous industrial discharges.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emission limits apply; office wastewater must comply with municipal sewerage ordinances; electronic waste disposal must follow MiAMBIENTE e-waste guidance; refrigeration and air-conditioning maintenance must avoid refrigerant leakage under applicable Montreal Protocol implementing regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety inspection, municipal land-use certificate, structural occupancy clearance for the leased office floor issued by a licensed engineer, and compliance with workplace safety and health requirements under Panamanian occupational regulations, including electrical safety, first-aid, and ergonomic workplace standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); online tax portal: DGI e-Tax 2.0 / SITIO (Sistema Integrado de Tributación en Línea), accessible via the official DGI website at www.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panama S.A. must procure a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) before carrying on any taxable activity. Procedure: (1) incorporate the Sociedad Anónima in the Registro Público de Panamá with a licensed resident agent (agente residente) and a resident legal representative (representante legal), and file beneficial-ownership information under Law 23 of 2015; (2) file the RUC application with the DGI through the resident agent, attaching the incorporation certificate (testimonio), corporate bylaws, resident-agent consent, registered-address evidence, and identification of directors and officers; (3) obtain the RUC certificate and a recognised digital-signature certificate (firma digital) for online filings; (4) activate the DGI online account and register the company as an ITBMS taxpayer with the relevant economic-activity code; (5) obtain the municipal aviso de operación (business permit) at the registered office and commence DGI-compliant electronic invoicing. The RUC is the single TIN/VAT identifier; foreign non-resident shareholders and directors do not require a Panamanian personal tax ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope; Entity_Level_Taxation. A Panama S.A. is a juridical person taxed at entity level exclusively on Panamanian-source income under the territoriality principle; foreign-source revenue, including ad-network payouts from Google AdMob and AppLovin derived from offshore platforms, falls outside the domestic income-tax base. ITBMS (VAT) applies to taxable transactions performed in or enjoyed within Panama, not to foreign-source export revenue. A standard S.A. is not a pass-through entity and cannot be disregarded for Panamanian tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election mechanism exists in Panamanian law. Statutory options available to the S.A.: (a) opt-in to the simplified small-taxpayer regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) where annual gross turnover is at or below approximately PAB 36,000, replacing the standard income-tax and ITBMS compliance burden with a simplified payment method; (b) election to register and operate as an export-services platform under Law 41 of 2007, which secures ITBMS zero-rating, territorial income-tax treatment and an enhanced export-documentation framework; (c) election of the monthly or quarterly filing calendar for ITBMS and income-tax advance returns according to the DGI duty roster; (d) no group or consolidated income-tax filing election is available for separate S.A. entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a las Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – Panamanian value-added tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB (Balboa, at par with USD) – There is no de minimis turnover threshold: any person habitually carrying out taxable transfers of goods or provisions of services in Panama must register for ITBMS before commencing operations, irrespective of revenue volume. A simplified compliance track is available for small taxpayers below approximately PAB 36,000 of annual gross income, but registration itself remains compulsory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) is phased in by the DGI and applies to the general taxpayer population. Invoices must be issued as digitally signed XML/UBL documents bearing DGI-authorized sequential numbering and transmitted to the DGI online validation platform; taxpayers must use DGI-certified billing software or the DGI free web issuer. High-volume issuers integrate through API/web-service clearance; a DGI acknowledgement (acuse de recibo) constitutes fiscal clearance. There is no physical fiscal stamp; legal validity depends on DGI digital validation. Non-validated invoices do not support input ITBMS credits and expose the issuer to fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and exported services are subject to ITBMS at 0%. A service qualifies as exported when rendered to a non-resident person for use, benefit, or enjoyment abroad. The S.A.'s revenue-share stream from AdMob and AppLovin (both foreign ad networks) qualifies: the contractual payees are non-resident, the game-publishing and ad-inventory services are delivered to offshore platforms, and the economic benefit is realized outside Panama. To claim 0% the taxpayer must evidence the foreign recipient, the offshore consumption of the service, and inbound remittance. Certification as an export-services platform under Law 41 of 2007 strengthens eligibility and provides a rebuttable presumption of export status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and bill of lading (required only for physical-goods exports; not applicable to pure digital service exports)
Executed digital services agreement or platform terms with Google (AdMob) and AppLovin identifying the foreign payer and revenue-share mechanics
Law 41 of 2007 export-services platform registration certificate (if the election is made)
Ad-network payout reports (AdMob and AppLovin statements) mapping gross revenue, deductions, and foreign remittance
Inward remittance certificate from a Panamanian bank evidencing receipt of USD from abroad
ITBMS sales register (libro de ventas) and periodic ITBMS returns presenting zero-rated lines separately
Annual income-tax return declaration classifying the revenue as foreign-source under the territoriality rules
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama is a dollarized economy with no exchange controls; there is no statutory FX repatriation deadline. However, DGI auditors routinely expect inward-remittance evidence within a 180-day window for each zero-rated invoice, and failure to demonstrate offshore receipt and foreign-source character can lead to denial of the 0% rate. On reassessment, the S.A. is liable for the full 7% ITBMS on gross payouts plus monthly default interest and fines generally ranging up to 100%–300% of the omitted tax, with higher sanctions for recidivism; fabrication of export documentation or sham foreign contracts triggers criminal tax-fraud charges under the Código Fiscal and AML liability under Law 23 of 2015. Retained foreign earnings not supported by payout reports may also be scrutinized for undisclosed Panamanian-source revenue.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP, Superintendency of Banks of Panama) — the sole banking conduct-of-business supervisor of the Republic of Panama; there is no central bank issuing domestic currency; the Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama) functions as fiscal agent for the Panamanian Treasury rather than as a monetary authority, while monetary stability is effectively delegated to the United States Federal Reserve through the statutory dollarization regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto currency convertibility. Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction: the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a purely nominal unit pegged 1:1 to the United States dollar (USD), and the USD is the legal tender used in all domestic transactions. There are no exchange controls, no mandatory conversion ratios, no central-bank approval for remittances, no FX licensing requirement, and no restriction on repatriation of dividends or return of capital; profits may be remitted freely through the SBP-regulated banking system. Under the territorial tax model, foreign-source gaming revenue derived from ad-monetization platforms (AdMob and AppLovin) is outside Panamanian source-income taxation pursuant to Article 694 of the Fiscal Code; dividend withholding tax of 5% applies only to distributions made out of Panamanian-source taxable profits. The only practical profit-remittance hurdles are documentary in nature: formal board and shareholder resolutions, RUA beneficial-ownership filings, and the annual fiduciary income-tax declaration (Form R068).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no percentage surrender obligation, and no mandatory conversion requirement on export proceeds, digital ad-monetization receipts, or any other foreign-exchange inflow. Because the domestic settlement currency is the USD, export receipts are immediately usable in-country without any repatriation formalities. The only compliance requirements in the vicinity are transaction reporting by the receiving bank to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) under Law 23 of 2015 when a single wire or an aggregate series exceeds USD 10,000, and the maintenance of ordinary commercial invoicing documentation to support territorial-source income characterization for the annual corporate tax file.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account plus capital-injection escrow sleeve
Operational USD account with regional Latin-American wire network
Capital escrow / fiduciary custody account (state-bank conservative posture)
Operational USD account for lean-treasury cross-border flows

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC International Bank, Inc. (BAC Credomatic Panama)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High, subject to material legal constraints. Panama's Fintech Law (Law 21 of April 20, 2021) created SBP-authorized e-money and innovation-sandbox licensing; offshore digital EMIs such as Payoneer, Airwallex, Wise, and similar wallet providers do not hold Panamanian banking licenses and may not establish branches or accept local deposits in Panama. A Panamanian S.A. may lawfully use such EMIs as settlement pass-through rails for AdMob and AppLovin payouts provided that (i) the EMI's contractual relationship is with the S.A. itself under an express treasury resolution, (ii) funds ultimately land in the SBP-licensed USD corporate account, and (iii) the UAF reporting thresholds are preserved through bank-side monitoring; nonetheless, the treasury blueprint must designate an SBP-licensed Tier-1 bank as the sole final custodian of corporate liquidity and must never leave the EMI as the primary repository of gaming proceeds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory, subject to a layered compromise for Low_Risk_Standard structures. All Tier-1 Panamanian banks require the S.A.'s legal representative (or a notarized Panamanian attorney-in-fact holding corporate power) to appear in person at a Panama City branch for the onboarding interview; fully remote account opening for a non-resident-owned S.A. is not viable in current SBP supervisory practice. A live videoconference interview of the ultimate beneficial owner may be accepted by Multibank and Banistmo if the attorney-in-fact appears physically, while Banco General and Global Bank generally require the UBO or the locally designated director to appear physically as well. Directors should budget a two-to-five day Panama City onboarding visit and engage local compliance counsel to chair the KYC interview and to pre-clear the ad-network revenue documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional red flag — a Panama S.A. with offshore directors, no visible local operations, and a nominee-shareholder profile is screened by bank-wide FATF systems as a potential tax-haven shell.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (a) the Registro Público Certificate of Incorporation and good-standing certificate, (b) the RUA beneficial-ownership extract naming each gaming investor, (c) a Memorandum of Engagement describing the hyper-casual mobile-game publishing activity with actual app titles, platform URLs, and global user statistics, (d) two years of IFRS/GAAP management accounts, (e) an independent auditor's report, (f) a client-acceptance note from the Panamanian law firm attesting to the corporate substance, and (g) a KYC questionnaire textually mapping the digital advertising payouts to revenue from services rather than financial intermediation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structuring suspicion — high-frequency fractional payouts from AdMob and AppLovin (daily or weekly net-30 settlements) resemble smurfing patterns to automated transaction-monitoring modules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (a) the platform-level revenue dashboard from AdMob and AppLovin MAX attributing every reported wire to specific app impressions and eCPM events, (b) MT940 end-of-day statements cross-referenced to the dashboard's received-payments ledger, (c) a treasury reconciliation workbook signed by the finance director, (d) an auditor's confirmation of aggregated impression counts, and (e) the internal AML playbook provisions requiring all ad-network receivables to flow solely through the SBP-licensed operating account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk counterparty hits — game-studio subcontractors or user territories identified as Russia, China, or OFAC-flagged jurisdictions produce alert entries in transaction monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (a) UAF/OFAC screening outputs and internal disposition notes for every flagged payee, (b) contractual representations and warranties on sanctions compliance embedded in each studio agreement, (c) the geo-blocking configuration report proving compliance with AdMob programme policies, (d) transaction-path maps demonstrating that no funds were sent to comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions, and (e) an independent third-party AML audit opinion covering the preceding twelve months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital surge — registered capital set near the statutory minimum of USD 10,001 and followed by a sudden multi-million-dollar inbound wire is interpreted as possible third-party capital infiltration or informal shell funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Furnish (a) notarized shareholders' subscription minutes approving the capital increase and the exact class of shares issued, (b) a bank-issued incoming-funds statement evidencing the remitter and routing, (c) an appraised valuation report for any capital-in-kind contribution of software code or game IP, (d) a sworn statement of economic means, (e) certified pages of the corporate share register (Registro de Acciones), and (f) board minutes instructing the bank to credit the capital-increase escrow sub-account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity routing requires a SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 CBPR+ pacs.009 for CBPR+-enabled banks) with beneficiary named as the exact Panama S.A. legal title and the narrative field reading 'Capital contribution / Suscripción de acciones'; Panama maintains no national FX-purpose-code table, but the SBP supervisory regime requires the receiving bank to document economic purpose at onboarding, so the remitter must pre-file the notarized shareholders' resolution authorizing the capital increase, the share-subscription register entries, the RUA declarations of the incoming investor, and source-of-wealth documentation covering the remitting entity; wires exceeding USD 10,000 are automatically reported by the receiving bank to the UAF; the injected funds should be parked in a bank-designated escrow sleeve until the bank completes its sample forensic screening, after which the funds are swept to the operational account without any FX conversion because the deposit is already USD-denominated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail is the SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer for revenue-share payments and third-party studio licensing commissions; for higher-value obligations such as consolidated publishing advances above USD 250,000, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit conforming to ICC UCP 600 and confirmed by the beneficiary's correspondent bank is the accepted mechanism; the local ACH clearing facility operated by the Asociación Bancaria de Panamá under SBP oversight handles domestic liquidity sweeps and sub-ledger transfers; inbound AdMob and AppLovin payouts are received through their respective sponsor banks and recollected directly into the SBP-licensed USD corporate account, eliminating any FX conversion step; downstream dividend repatriation or parent-company payments are executed as ordinary SWIFT MT103 wires under pre-filed corporate minutes and standard tax-withholding certificates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (USD/BRL, USD/MXN, USD/EUR) with tenors up to twelve months executed via SBP-licensed banks such as Banco General, Multibank, or Banistmo on ISDA 2002 terms

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-deliverable Latin American currencies (ARS, COP, CLP, VES) settled in USD through licensed offshore counterparties, reflecting the absence of local deliverability for those currencies

Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) for structurally converting foreign-currency revenue exposure (BRL/MXN) into USD-linked liabilities, executed under a bank swap desk or the parent-group treasury master agreement
European plain-vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars on USD/BRL and USD/MXN to cap seasonally spiked foreign-currency operating and user-acquisition costs

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation is the core incentive: a Panamanian S.A. is taxed only on Panama-source income, so foreign-source ad-network proceeds (AdMob/AppLovin) attributable to users, servers and activities outside Panama may be excluded from ISR. Available statutory incentives: (i) 10% reduced ISR bracket for small enterprises with net taxable income up to B/. 200,000; (ii) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007 (qualifying regional HQ services); (iii) Panama-Pacifico Special Economic Area and City of Knowledge exemptions; (iv) reforestation, tourism and agribusiness incentives. For hyper-casual gaming publishers, the 0% effective rate on net foreign-source profits is the primary planning feature, but the territorial-source claim requires documentary segregation of Panamanian end-users (which would be Panama-source).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 201 – Declaración de Renta (Impuesto sobre la Renta) for juridical persons, filed electronically through the DGI E-Tax 2.0 portal (https://etax.dgi.gob.pa) and the SAPI (Sistema de Administración de Ingresos Públicos) platform of the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year generally follows the calendar year (1 January – 31 December). The annual Form 201 is due on or before 15 March of the year immediately following the tax year end; quarterly advance ISR payments are due in April, June, September and December during the tax year (exact dates per DGI resolutions, normally the fifteenth day of the month). A company that merely holds a RUC but reports no taxable activity must still file and submit a nil or informational declaration to avoid administrative cancellation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 201-01 – RUC and taxpayer identification data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) number, fiscal period, business activity code (ISIC 5820) and taxpayer status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the RUC is active and the Aviso de Operación is renewed annually. A foreign-owned S.A. with no activity must file the corresponding nil declaration in each period to keep the status valid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Caja 1 – Ingresos brutos de fuente panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues from sales of goods or services rendered, used, or economically exploited within Panama, including in-app purchases and ad revenues from Panamanian end-users.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate Panama-source revenue from foreign-source revenue at geo level. Include only Panama-source receipts in Caja 1; keep geo/IP evidence from ad networks for audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Caja 2 – Ingresos de fuente extranjera y exentos
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenues derived from outside Panama (foreign end-users, offshore servers, foreign royalties) and income exempt under specific statutory regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the total foreign-source ad-network proceeds and attach a geo-activity schedule with supporting payment statements from AdMob/AppLovin; the taxpayer bears the burden of proving the foreign source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary business expenses attributable to the production of taxable Panama-source income, supported by invoices and bank records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident managed S.A., keep costs allocable to foreign-source revenue outside the Panamanian tax calculation; avoid cross-allocating generic HQ costs to Panama in a manner that creates a Panamanian PE exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions and NOL carryforwards (maximum 5-year carryforward for losses sustained in Panama-source operations).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NOLs may only offset Panama-source income; foreign-source losses do not reduce Panama taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting corporate income tax at 25% applied to Caja 11 (or 10% bracket if the small-enterprise conditions are met).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the taxable base is zero or negative, indicate the nil result; compute the CAIR minimum payment (advance corporate tax) if applicable to large taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Caja 13 – Anticipos y retenciones del período
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly advance payments, withholding taxes suffered in Panama, and any special tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match advance payments made to the RUC; retain DGI receipts. Non-resident companies generally have no Panamanian withholding credits on foreign ad revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Caja 14 – Saldo a pagar o saldo a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after credits, or carryforward credit if overpaid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle any payable via the E-Tax bank payment module by the deadline; overpayment refunds require a separate DGI application and desktop audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty of 5% of the tax due for each commenced month of delay, up to a maximum of 25%; for nil returns, a fixed administrative penalty (approximately B/. 50–B/. 500) is imposed. Late payment additionally triggers a 10% surcharge on the unpaid tax plus moratory interest calculated from the original due date. Repeated failure to file can lead to suspension of the RUC, blocking of imports, refusal of banking operations, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (dividend tax) applies to distributions made out of profits not previously subject to ISR at the corporate level, including distributions of foreign-source profits; 0% if the profits have borne the 25% ISR at the S.A. level. Dividends paid to residents and non-residents are subject to the same rule; the Panama payer withholds the final tax at the moment the dividend is declared or paid. Profits distributed to shareholders of a conducting company under the small-enterprise regime are typically subject to a 5% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama applies DTAs only where the treaty has been signed, ratified, and published in the Gaceta Oficial. To invoke a reduced rate: (i) the beneficial-owner shareholder obtains a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of its residence jurisdiction, translated into Spanish and apostilled/baptized as required; (ii) the payee delivers the TRC, a DTA self-certification/beneficial-ownership declaration and (where requested) a legal-opinion memorandum to the Panamanian withholding agent before the payment date; (iii) the withholding agent applies the treaty rate at source and files the withholding return through E-Tax with the supporting documents retained in the tax file; (iv) the DGI may require submission of the original TRC within 30 calendar days; improper claims expose the payer to solidary liability for the under-withheld tax plus interests and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: payments made by a Panamanian S.A. for rights used in Panama are Panama-source and subject to statutory 12.5% withholding tax (computed as 25% on a presumptive 50% net base); DTA rates commonly range between 5% and 10%. Interest: interest paid to a non-resident lender on credit raised abroad is generally not subject to Panama withholding tax; treaty rates, where applicable, usually range from 5% to 10%. The DGI will recharacterize excessive, back-to-back or thinly capitalized interest payments as constructive royalties or equity distributions, exposing them to the 10% dividend tax or 12.5% royalty WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 3,000,000 (US$3,000,000) of annual gross revenue or B/. 1,500,000 of aggregate related-party transactions in a fiscal year; taxpayers exceeding the thresholds must prepare a Local File, Master File (when the consolidated group exceeds the DGI threshold) and file the annual transfer-pricing schedule with the Form 201 documentation package. Even below the threshold, the DGI can require analysis for specific controlled transactions, and the documentation must be delivered within 45 business days of a formal request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not operate a BVI/Cayman-style Economic Substance (Amendment) regime for the standard S.A. However, the territorial-source claim and the 10% dividend tax create a de facto substance test: the DGI will scrutinize whether management and control, personnel, decision-making, servers, and the geo-location of end-users support a foreign-source characterization. For a hyper-casual gaming S.A., creditable substance includes: substantive technical staff and development activity of the group outside Panama, centralized treasury and commercial management away from Panamanian territory, and no Panamanian employees, premises or signatories with authority to execute material contracts. Additionally, Law 129 of 2020 and its implementing Beneficial Ownership Register (RBF) require the S.A. to identify natural-person beneficial owners; RBF non-compliance results in restriction of corporate rights, suspension of dividend distributions, and administrative fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False or misleading ISR declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Panama-source ad revenues, inventing deductible costs, or presenting a fabricating foreign-source segregation to reduce the 25% ISR base; using nominee companies to hide the true Panamanian beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative: fine up to 100% of the omitted tax plus moratory interest and the 25% late-filing cap; civil claim for the total tax shortfall. Criminal: evasion of taxes through false declarations constitutes defraudación tributaria (Código Penal, Article 289-A, as amended in 2019), punishable with imprisonment of 2 to 4 years, increased to 4 to 6 years where the evaded amount exceeds B/. 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, administrators and signatories who knowingly approve or sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and exposed to criminal prosecution, patrimonial embargo, travel bans and disqualification from serving as corporate officers or obtaining public contracts in Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Gapless Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the S.A. as an empty shell with no demonstrable activity, no bank account, no records and no registered economic narrative; failing to file the Beneficial Ownership Register (RBF) or renew the Aviso de Operación; claiming blanket foreign-source exclusion while all directors, bank signatories and the registered agent operate from Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RBF non-compliance: fines in the range of B/. 1,000 to B/. 50,000 per filing violation and temporary suspension of the shareholder dividend rights; Aviso de Operación non-renewal leads to cancellation of the RUC and eventual dissolution proceedings. The DGI may disregard the corporate form and recharacterize foreign-source profits as Panama-source, assessing 25% ISR plus interest; undistributed untaxed profits become subject to the 10% dividend tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the veil is pierced for fraud or abuse, directors are personally liable for corporate tax debts and fines. The Tax Court (Tribunal Administrativo Tributario) may order travel bans and embargo of personal assets during concealment audits, and criminal prosecution for falsification of books can result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering / AML-FT Violations in Cross-Border Payment Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving AdMob/AppLovin payouts through undisclosed nominee accounts, opaque factoring companies, or layered fintech intermediaries without commercial justification; failing to apply KYC/beneficial-ownership identification to the receiving account; structuring cash flows to avoid the B/. 10,000 cash-reporting or the 10% dividend tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT), which can reach B/. 1,000,000 for serious violations; criminal money laundering (Código Penal) carries imprisonment of 5 to 10 years for simple laundering, increased to 5 to 15 years where organized structures or repeated transactions are proven; instrumentalities and proceeds are subject to confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly design opaque payment structures face personal criminal liability, asset forfeiture, travel bans, and 5-year disqualification from managing financial or corporate entities in Panama; banks may also blacklist the officers individually.
